To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the backbone dynamics of the glucocoicoid receptor DNA‐Binding Domain (GRDBD) are rather limited, and that there are only a few residues that exhibit a more large‐ scale motion.

the experimental 15N N‐MR relaxation data can be interpreted with a molecular dynamics trajectory of the protein and that the backbone dynamics is rather limited and uniform, with a somewhat decreased flexibility for the two α‐helices.

the experimental 15N relaxation parameters are reproduced by a 200 ps molecular dynamics simulation of GR DBD, that the backbone motions are rather uniform and that the motions of the backbone in the zinc‐binding regions are slightly different from the motions in the rest of the protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular basis of the interaction of glucocorticoid receptors (GR) with their target DNA.
the development of a new class of compounds for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease.
the study of protein dynamics using a combination of molecular dynamics simulations and experimental NMR relaxation studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the experimental and simulated relaxation data were in good agreement, and that the simulation reproduced most of the experimental features, including the large differences in mobility for the different parts of the protein.
the backbone motions in the GR DBD are rather limited and that the motions that are observed are well represented by an isotropic reorientation with an effective correlation time of 2.3 nsec.
the experimental and simulated data are in good agreement and thus that the molecular dynamics simulation of GR DBD is able to reproduce the observed rapid backbone motions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experimental data are consistent with a picture of the protein as a rigid body with a limited internal flexibility.

the experimental data were in good agreement with the simulation, and thus that the simulation reproduced the experimental data, but that there were some differences in the time scales of the motions that were dominating the experimental and simulated data.

the backbone of the glucocorticoide receptor DNA‐binding domains is rather rigid and that the motions of the backbone are limited to local motions, except for a few residues in the extended and zinc‐binding regions, which are subject to more large‐scale motions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of experimental NMR data and molecular simulation can be very powerful in the characterization of the dynamics of biomacromolecules.
the backbone dynamics of the glucorticoid receptor DNA binding domain (DBD) is rather uniform throughout the structure.
it is important to consider the time scales of motions when comparing experimental and simulated data.
